alignments.note: Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate adjective, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 20).

CORRECTED. The impersonal 'it' anticipating the ʾăšer clause is not the presentative dummy rule 20 hands to a predicate: that rule governs the presentative 'there' and no other, and says explicitly that a cleft or impersonal 'it' — as in 'It is enough' — is licensed by no morpheme and is its own added unit under rule 30. The competing reading folds it into the predicate adjective with the copula.

review_notes: Correction: the impersonal 'it' of 'Better is it' was split off as its own added unit. The clause's predication is the written adjective ṭôb, which keeps the construction-supplied copula under rule 20, but that rule limits the construction-supplied dummy to the presentative 'there' and marks a cleft or impersonal 'it' added.
This is not rule 20's cleft frame either: the predication is carried by the predicate adjective the Hebrew writes, so only the dummy subject is unlicensed and the copula stays with ṭôb.
